name: Electrician

pf.license.need: Electrical work in a home needs a license where the state, city or county licenses electricians. Some states license by job size or kind of work, like residential-only or limited licenses.
pf.license.who holds it: Both: the company (an electrical contractor license, where the state asks) and each electrician (apprentice, journeyman or master, where the state licenses people).
what to ask: The company's license number and class
Each electrician's own number and level, in their invite reply
The local license for the job's city or county, where only cities or counties license home electrical work
Any specialty license and its limits, like low voltage, solar or signs: from the state form
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: The company's electrical listing goes live once it's set up. Each electrician is offered only once the owner says yes.
pf.license.job limits: Where a license stops at a job size or a kind of work, each quote and extra job is checked against it before it's sent.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks (the example: 5 weeks and 1 week before). A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.lead-safe work: Cutting into painted walls or ceilings in an older home: a lead-safe certified firm and worker, where the rules require it.
pf.license.at the counter: Lamps and fixtures brought to the shop counter are cord-and-plug work, not wiring in a building: the state's form says if it needs a license. Safe default: the company's license on file, shown on the listing.
pf.license.local rules: Where only a city or county licenses home electrical work, the license for the job's address is the one checked.

pf.services.capacity: One electrician per home visit. A panel replacement or a long trench can need a crew of two. The counter: one lamp tech per booking, and its one test bench for antique lamps.
pf.services.skills each needs: EV chargers and panel work need the skill the owner names. Antique lamps at the counter need the antique skill. Solar work needs its own license where the state asks.
pf.services.nobody home: Outdoor work with its own access, like a yard light or an outside outlet: nobody needs to be home. DONE comes with a photo.
pf.services.online: A video check only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at cost or at list, the owner's pick. Permit fees shown on the quote. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

stops the booking.words: Smoke, sparks, a burning smell, or a hot panel, outlet or switch
stops the booking.says: Get everyone out, and don't touch the panel. Call 911 from outside.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until the fire department says the home is safe. The customer can come back then.

stops the booking.words: A downed or sparking power line
stops the booking.says: Stay at least 30 feet away, and keep others away. Call the power company's emergency line, or 911 if it's sparking or anyone is hurt.
stops the booking.booking: No booking now. Damage on the house's side, like the meter box or the pipe the wires come in through, is booked once the power company makes it safe.

stops the booking.words: Someone got a shock or is hurt
stops the booking.says: Don't touch them if they may still be touching power. Call 911.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

stops the booking.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas company.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water near outlets, a light or the panel
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Stay away from the water and anything plugged in. Don't touch a switch or the panel while standing in water. Switch off that breaker only from a dry spot.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A breaker that won't reset, or power out in part of the home
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Don't keep resetting it. Unplug what's on that circuit. If you smell burning, get out and call 911.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A lamp or cord that sparked (at the counter)
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Unplug it and don't use it. Bring it in, or book a home visit if it's wired into the house.

pf.safety.a fix the customer declines: A hazard left as it is: the circuit is switched off and labeled, and the customer gets a written safety note not to use it. The note stays with the job.
pf.safety.at the counter: A light that's still wired into the house isn't worked on at the counter. Taking it down or putting it up is a home visit.
pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the electrician, with a photo.
pf.visit.check-in at the counter: The code at the counter (the lamp tech or the desk types it). A drop-off gets its code when the item is left, and READY when it's tested.
pf.visit.quotes at the visit: The electrician texts the quote with its lines before any work. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.extra work: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A bigger job, like a panel, gets its own quote.
pf.visit.a fix declined: If the customer says no to a fix for a hazard, the electrician leaves that circuit off and labeled, and Rosie texts the written safety note.
pf.visit.work sold at the home: A written right to cancel, where the rules require it. The work starts at once only if the customer asks for that in writing, where the rules allow it.
pf.visit.old parts: The replaced parts are offered to the customer, where the state's rules require it.
pf.visit.before work: Photos of the panel and the work area before work; the year the home was built before opening a wall.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The electrician texts DONE with the bill's lines, and photos after. Nobody home needed: DONE with a photo.
pf.visit.permits: Where a permit was pulled, the inspection is set up after the work, and the power company turns the power back on where it shut it off. The result is kept with the job.

pf.staff.levels: Apprentice (or trainee), journeyman and master; each person's own license per state, where the state licenses electricians.
skills: Solar (its own license where the state asks)
pf.staff.supervision: An apprentice works only with a journeyman or master on the job, where the state's rules require it. An apprentice is never sent alone by default.
pf.staff.special work: Panel work only by a master electrician or a person the owner names. A specialty or limited license limits what that person may be booked for. Lead-safe work only by people with the lead-safe card, where the rules require it.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, panel jobs and same-day jobs. After hours, a job sent now goes to the electrician on call, then the backup set at sign-up. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another electrician with the same skill and level, at the same window and price.

pf.rules.written contract: A signed written contract before work above an amount, and no money before it's signed: from the state form.
pf.rules.right to cancel: A written right to cancel for work sold at the home: where the rules require it.
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the license holder where the local rules require one; the inspection follows.
pf.rules.power company: The power company's shut-off and turn-on for a panel swap or a service change.
pf.rules.lead-safe work: Lead-safe work rules for older homes: where the rules require it.
pf.rules.license on papers: The license number on listings, confirmations, quotes and bills: from the state form.
pf.rules.one service charge: One service charge per visit, shown before the customer agrees: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.old parts: Offer the customer the replaced parts: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.digging: A utility locate before any digging: always.
pf.rules.declared emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own (the example: 1 year on labor), shown on the receipt.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for electrical work:
electrical: Smoke, sparks or a burning smell at any point: stop, get everyone out, call 911
A downed power line: 30 feet away, and call the power company
The problem gets worse before the visit: the safety steps again, then urgent
After hours: sent now to the electrician on call, then the backup; nobody takes it means no visit tonight and the hold released
A fix for a hazard declined: the circuit left off and labeled, with a written safety note
A bigger job found, like a scorched panel: its own quote, OK'd by the owner over the limit, with its permit
A panel swap: the permit, the power company's shut-off and turn-on, and the inspection before the last stage is billed
A quote past what the license allows: not sent, and the owner is told
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A renter whose landlord pays: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead
A storm brings many outage calls: PAUSE, and a declared emergency's price limits
At the counter: a lamp that can't be fixed safely, a light still wired in, or a drop-off nobody picks up

notes:
Pilot: the plumber (pattern fix). An electrician runs the same way: a home visit in a 2-hour arrival window, the service call held and taken off the repair, a quote at the visit, permits, and someone on call after hours. Its counter side gives flow A. Unlike the plumber, the master's flow B story is plumbing, so every plumbing word there is renamed to electrical work (about 570 rename pairs, built the way the locksmith's are).
Flow B: Lee Home Services becomes Highline Electric (the old flowchart's business); Jordan becomes Darnell and Casey becomes Wes (male names, since the master's texts say he and him for both); 42 Oak St becomes 31 Birch Ln.
Flow B's services keep the master's numbers, one for one: the $179 drain clearing is a kitchen outlet repair (the old flowchart's dead kitchen outlets); the leak repair quoted at the visit is a breaker repair (a breaker that keeps tripping); the $150 water heater flush is a generator tune-up, also the yearly plan; the $640 water heater replacement from photos is an EV charger install (photos of the panel and the garage, a 25% deposit, a contract, a permit, delivery and setup); the $199/$249 sewer camera inspection is an electrical safety inspection with a report; the $2,400 repipe in 3 stages is a panel replacement from an estimate visit; the yard drain is a yard light line (outdoor, nobody home, a trencher, the weather); the faucet taken to the shop is a chandelier to rewire; the drying fan is a loaner generator; the shutoff valves are two scorched outlets; the drain trap is a light switch.
The master's second kind of work (electrical) becomes solar: Highline Solar, with a solar installer whose license is checked before it goes live. Solar is a common pair for electrical contractors, and it reads as a noun the way the master uses 'electrical'. The rename runs the master's electrical words first (to solar), then plumbing to electrical, so nothing is renamed twice.
Flow A, the less usual side: Sam's second company (the master's Lee's Barbershop) is Highline Lamp Shop, a lamp and light repair counter where a customer brings a lamp, a chandelier or a fixture in. It loads the electrical plug-in's counter side. Riley becomes Nina (only Nina does antique lamps) and Avery becomes Hank; 88 Elm St becomes 16 Canal St.
The counter's example prices keep the master's amounts: lamp rewire $35, new cord and plug $40, new switch $20, holiday light repair $25, floor lamp rewire $55 (paid in full), chandelier rewire $140 (2½ hours: a card saved for the $40 fee, a $40 deposit, or a drop-off), antique lamp restore from photos $90, lamp repair priced at the counter after a $25 bench check, a home visit $75. These are examples, not facts about prices.
The master's barbershop words get their counter version: the patch test is a parts check (the antique lamp brought in first, so the right old-style parts can be ordered); color work is antique lamps; the perm the shop doesn't do is a TV repair; the gloss on a quote is a new harp; the cape clip is the bench vise; the towel steamer is the lamp tester.
Lamps at a counter are cord-and-plug work, not wiring in a building, so whether they're licensed is the state form's call. S1-63 and S2-28 keep both branches; the example state licenses the shop and each lamp tech, worded 'where Sam is'.
Safety first (pf.safety): smoke, sparks, a burning smell or a hot panel, outlet or switch stops the booking (get everyone out, call 911 from outside, book again once the fire department says the home is safe). A downed power line: 30 feet away, the power company, 911 if it's sparking or anyone is hurt; damage on the house's side is booked once the power company makes it safe. Water near outlets, a light or the panel gets safety steps, then the booking goes on, marked urgent. A breaker that won't reset: don't keep resetting it.
Flow B safety ops: the power line on B3-19 (more), the safety words again when nobody on call can come (B6-18 more), and sparks at the visit (B8-30 more). The master's own safety examples (Rosa's call, the problem that gets worse, the hazard behind the wall) are renamed to electrical ones: water dripping onto a ceiling light, kitchen lights going out too, scorched old wiring behind the kitchen wall with its circuit left off and labeled.
A fix the customer declines for a hazard: the circuit stays off and labeled, and a written safety note goes out (B8-21 more, the plug-in). The master lacks this for every trade: gap.
Old parts offered back, where the state's rules require it: B8-39 (more) and a pf.rules switch. Gap.
Panel swaps: the permit to-do also asks for the power company's shut-off and turn-on dates (B4-42 more), and the power comes back on once the city passes it (B10-24 more). The master has the inspection, not the utility: gap.
Money, flow B: main list|hold|bill, the plug-in's starting answer (a card saved for the $89 service call fee, Rosie texts the bill). The old flowchart took nothing up front and sent a $95 fee by pay link, so list|none|bill and visit|none|bill are listed; with nothing taken the master charges no fee (S11-30), which is why the hold is the starting answer. list|card|bill, visit|card|bill and list|card|card are for owners who save a card; photos|deposit|bill is the EV charger; list|full|none is the generator tune-up. No deposit on visit-priced work, and no business's-own-way billing.
Money, flow A: the counter's set, as the plumber's: list|card|counter main, plus nothing taken, the $40 hold, the $40 deposit, the full price, priced from photos, and priced at the counter.
The old flowchart's $95 service call is the master's $89 here, so every sum and fee stays right.
keep: electrical and electrician (this profession's own words, which are also on the master's list of example words) and service call (the old flowchart's own word).
Plug-in splits, the same decisions as the plumber's. Both flows: the $2, no added agreement, people not spaces, no classes, work sent now (an after-hours outage); the license splits S1-60, S1-63 and S2-28 kept whole. Flow A: walk-ins wait in a line or a drop-off is checked in at once; a lamp tech's time or a chandelier drop-off slot; adults only; no form, no damage hold, no crew, no date that can't move, no minimum; late means a shorter visit or the next open time; rated. Flow B: arrival windows only; own or rent asked; no damage hold at booking; one electrician by name or a crew of two; no group minimum; an adult must be there when a child answers.
splitsKept, flow A: S1-60, S1-63, S2-28; A7-59, S11-87, S11-90 (a chandelier drop-off names no lamp tech); A7-61 (antique lamps are Nina's alone); A8-02 (a rewire needs the lamp with its parts); A8-53 (the counter, or a drop-off). Flow B: S1-60, S1-63, S2-28; B4-81, B7-55, B8-58 (an after-hours outage is sent now, an EV charger never); B4-57 (a written contract over the state form's amount); B8-69, B8-70 (a yard light with nobody home); B8-71 (an EV charger delivered and set up); B8-65 (a panel replacement's inspection partway); B10-29 (the permit inspection after); B8-72 (a chandelier to the shop).
Flow A ops: a video check (A4-36 more), a lamp that sparks at home before the visit (A7-13 words), a lamp that can't be rewired safely (A8-x01, a new branch on A8-32), a chandelier drop-off while Nina is out (A7-60 words) and the drop-off slots (A4-67). The rush (A4-29) and the landlord's five lamps (A4-32) are rename pairs on the master's own sentences, so they need no op.
The master's bigger job found at the visit (B8-27) is Alex asking about an EV charger at the outlet visit, priced from photos as its own job; on the EV charger path it's a panel too small for the charger ($900). The old flowchart's panel found at the visit is the master's estimate that becomes its own job (B8-62: Harper's $2,400 panel replacement).
No state is named: licenses (state, city or county), job-size limits, permits, lead-safe work, contracts and money before the work, deposit caps, one service charge, old parts, cancel days and emergency prices are switches filled from each state's form. The old flowchart's Ohio, Pennsylvania, California and Texas rules applied everywhere are OUTDATED.
Outdated: Housecall Pro, Jobber, ServiceTitan, Rosie Book and Rosie Calendar as separate tools, and the QuickBooks export. Rosie is the business's software now; only the phone calendar and Stripe connect.
Review (Oct 22): flow A's plan and insurance branches off at the counter (A4-28, A4-54, A7-02, A9-15: they showed an eye exam's lens fitting), and A10-06's rented items off; the plug-in's starting answers now name the saved card charged at DONE (B list|card|card) and, at the counter, nothing taken or a $40 deposit (A list|none|counter, list|deposit|counter); S11-58's second kind of work at the lamp shop is appliance repair.
Touch-up Oct 22: the master's "package cut" now reads "rewire from a package" (A5-04, A5-13, A5-16), matching A5-03 ("Uses a rewire from Alex's package"), instead of "package repair".
touch-up 4 (Oct 23): keep 'heater': 'don't run two heaters on one circuit' is a real electrician's tip (space heaters trip breakers).
